description: Student error d1_01: the returned weights are 1e-7 away from the optimum (an iteration stopped too early), so the stationarity residual is about 1e-7, above the 1e-8 tolerance.

Student error d1_02: the turnover multipliers are assigned by the sign of each displacement (plus if w_i is above w0_i, minus if below), not by the sign constraint the solver used, so the stationarity in the turnover variables fails at zero displacement.
Student error d1_03: the weights sum to one plus 5e-9 (inside the 1e-8 tolerance), and the certificate reports a primal residual of exactly zero instead of recomputing it from the weights.

Student error d1_04: the certificate's turnover-variable stationarity is reported as the total multiplier kappa alone, dropping the plus and minus multipliers, so it is non-zero whenever the turnover limit binds.
Student error d2_01: asset i is placed in sector i mod Z instead of the sector label the case gives it, so every sector cap applies to the wrong assets.

Student error d2_02: the complementary-slackness residual evaluates the two turnover rows at t = 0 (d_i and minus d_i) instead of at t_i = |d_i|, so a binding turnover multiplier is reported as a slackness violation.
Student error d2_03: the active-set rule drops a working constraint only when its multiplier is negative and it is a bound or sector row, so a negative turnover multiplier stays in the answer.
Student error d3-01: the certificate subtracts the sector multiplier in the weight stationarity, so the sector term enters with the wrong sign.
Student error d3-02: the upper bounds w_i <= u_i are left out of the active-set search, so an answer can exceed a bound.
Student error d3-03: the turnover limit is relaxed by 1e-7, so the total change from the starting portfolio can exceed the limit by more than the 1e-8 tolerance.
Student error d3-04: the certificate evaluates the turnover complementary-slackness rows at t_i = |w_i| instead of t_i = |w_i - w0_i|.
Student error f01: gamma equal to 1e-6 is refused, so the valid boundary is lost.
Student error f02: an upper bound equal to the starting weight is refused as if it were below it.
Student error f03: a lower bound equal to the starting weight is refused as if the start lay below it.
Student error f04: a sector cap equal to the starting sector weight is refused.
Student error f05: the starting sum is checked only from above, so a sum short of one by 2e-9 is accepted.
Student error f06: symmetry is checked to a tolerance of 1e-3, so a 1e-4 asymmetry is accepted.
Student error f07: a missing sector_caps field is replaced by a cap of one per sector, and the answer is returned.
Student error f08: a turnover limit of minus 1e-6 is accepted, so only a clearly negative limit is refused.
Student error f09: a sector cap with no asset in it is accepted and never checked.
Student error f10: a boolean sector label is read as the integer it equals and accepted.
Student error f6_01: the budget multiplier is returned as the text of its value, not as a number.
Student error f6_02: the total turnover multiplier is returned as the text of its value, not as a number.
Student error f6_03: every lower-bound multiplier is returned as the text of its value, not as a number.
Student error f6_04: every upper-bound multiplier is returned as the text of its value, not as a number.
Student error f6_05: every sector multiplier is returned as the text of its value, not as a number.
Student error f6_06: every turnover-plus multiplier is returned as the text of its value, not as a number.
Student error f6_07: every turnover-minus multiplier is returned as the text of its value, not as a number.
Student error f6_08: the lower-bound multipliers are returned as booleans, true where the multiplier is non-zero.
Student error f6_09: the turnover-minus multipliers are returned as complex numbers with a zero imaginary part.
Student error f6_10: the last sector-cap multiplier is returned as None, the other sector entries as numbers.
Student error g2_01: the weights are returned as complex numbers, with a zero imaginary part.
Student error g2_02: the weights are returned as booleans (held or not held) instead of numbers.
Student error g2_03: the weights are returned as text strings.
Student error g2_04: the last weight is left as None when the solver has no value for it.
Student error g2_05: each weight is rounded to the nearest integer before it is returned.
Student error g2_06: the weights are rounded to denominators of at most 1000 and returned as Fractions.
Student error g2_07: the last weight is reported as NaN after the solve.
Student error g2_08: the weights are returned as a tuple instead of a list.
Student error g2_09: the primal residual is returned as a text string in the certificate.
Student error g2_10: the weights are returned as decimal.Decimal values, which the page does not name.
Student error m01: the lower bounds are left out of the constraint rows, so short sales are allowed where the box forbids them.
Student error m02: the turnover limit is measured from zero, not from the starting portfolio w0.
Student error m03: the active-set rule drops positive multipliers instead of negative ones, so dual feasibility is never enforced.
Student error m04: the quadratic term is written as gamma w' Sigma w, so the Hessian is 2 gamma Sigma (a factor-two convention error).
Student error m05: the answer for seed 0 is hard-coded and returned for every case.
Student error m06: the turnover limit is halved when the sign constraints are built, so trades are cut too early.
Student error m07: the sector caps are not imposed, so a sector can exceed its cap.
Student error m08: the budget multiplier is reported with the wrong sign, so the weight equations fail.
Student error m09: the expected returns enter the gradient with the wrong sign, so the portfolio chases the lowest returns.
Student error m10: the plus and minus turnover multipliers are reported the other way round.
Student error m11: a NaN in the lower bounds is read as zero instead of being refused with ValueError.
Student error m12: the starting portfolio's sector caps are checked with a tolerance of 1e-7, where the page states 1e-9.
Student error m13: the symmetry test of Sigma only catches an upper entry that is too large, so a lower entry that is too large is accepted.
Student error m14: the sector label range check tests only the upper end, so a label of minus one is accepted.
Student error m15: a bound with lower equal to upper is refused, so the boundary case is wrongly rejected.
Student error m16: a turnover limit of exactly zero is refused, though the page says it is valid.
Student error m17: the positive-definiteness test accepts a zero pivot, so a singular Sigma is accepted.
Student error m18: a risk aversion of exactly zero is accepted, because the check tests only for negative values.
Student error m19: the starting-portfolio sum is checked with a tolerance of 1e-6, where the page states 1e-9.
Student error m20: a boolean where a number belongs is accepted as 1 or 0, so gamma equal to True is solved.
Student error m21: a float sector label such as 0.0 is accepted and truncated to an integer.
Student error m22: a starting portfolio with one entry too many is silently truncated instead of refused.
Student error m23: a row of Sigma with one entry too many is silently truncated instead of refused.
Student error m24: a NaN expected return is replaced by zero instead of being refused with ValueError.
Student error p01: the starting weight is checked against its box for asset 0 only.
Student error p02: a lower bound above its upper bound is refused for asset 0 only.
Student error p03: a boolean sector label is accepted, because True counts as the integer one.
Student error p04: a float sector label is accepted at the last asset and truncated to an integer.
Student error p05: a boolean or text entry is refused only where its name ends in index 0; elsewhere it is read as a number.
Student error p06: the starting portfolio is checked against the sector cap of sector 0 only.
Student error p07: an instance that is not a mapping raises TypeError, where the page names ValueError.
Student error p08: a lower bound equal to the starting weight is refused as if the start lay below it.
Student error p09: the starting-portfolio box check skips the middle asset, asset 1.
Student error p10: the sector-label loop stops one short, so the last asset's label is never checked.
Student error q01: the upper-bound multiplier enters the certificate's weight stationarity with a minus sign.
Student error q02: a missing case field raises KeyError, where the page names ValueError for a missing field.
Student error q03: the certificate's gradient uses gamma / 2 in the quadratic term, a factor-two error.
Student error r01: the lower and upper bound multipliers enter the weight stationarity with swapped signs.
Student error r03: the plus multiplier enters the turnover-variable stationarity with a plus sign.
Student error r10_01: the sector multipliers are reported divided by the number of assets in their sector, a per-asset convention the page does not use.
Student error r10_02: the budget multiplier is read off asset 0 alone, as mu[0] minus gamma times the first row of Sigma times w, ignoring every other multiplier in that row.
Student error r10_03: the lower-bound multipliers are never reported; the output lists zero for every asset, so the weight stationarity fails wherever a lower bound binds.

Student error: the turnover multipliers are split as the positive and negative parts of the net sign multiplier (plus = max(net, 0), minus = max(-net, 0)) instead of (kappa +/- net) / 2, so kappa - plus - minus is not zero.
Student error: the solver raises once the working set holds n - 1 inequality rows (a vertex, with the budget), so every answer that the bounds pin to a vertex is refused.
Student error: the turnover limit is enforced only through the 2**(n-1) sign forms whose first entry is +1, so the sign constraints of the other orthants are never imposed.
Student error: the sector caps are read in reverse order, so sector k is bounded by the cap of sector Z-1-k.
Student error r12-01: the gradient is Sigma w minus mu, with the risk aversion gamma left out of the quadratic term.
Student error r12-04: the reported turnover_total is the sum of the plus multipliers, not the multiplier of the total turnover constraint.
Student error r12-05: the search stops at the first stationary point and never drops a constraint with a negative multiplier.
Student error r13_01: the weights are rounded to six decimal places before they are reported.
Student error r13_02: the budget (equality) multiplier is put in the dual-feasibility list as if it were an inequality multiplier.
Student error r13_03: the stationarity expression in the weights leaves out the sector-cap multiplier term.
Student error r14_01: the weight stationarity leaves out the turnover plus and minus multipliers.
Student error r14_02: the weight stationarity subtracts the budget multiplier instead of adding it.
Student error r14_03: the certificate's gradient omits the risk-aversion factor gamma.
Student error r14_04: the stationarity uses the multiplier of sector 0 for every asset.
Student error r14_05: the lower-bound multipliers are reported from the upper-bound list.
Student error r14_06: the turnover-total multiplier is reported as the sum of the plus multipliers.
Student error r14_07: the weights are rounded to four decimal places before they are returned.
Student error r14_08: allocate returns an extra status key beside the three fields of the page.
Student error r14_09: the multiplier for the total turnover is named turnover_sum, not turnover_total.
Student error r14_10: the turnover sign constraints are offset by minus the starting portfolio, not plus it.
Student error r15-01: the turnover is summed over the positive deviations only (max(d, 0)), so a sell from w0 costs nothing.
Student error r15-02: the weight stationarity uses sigma w - mu and forgets the risk-aversion factor gamma.
Student error r15-03: the starting-portfolio tolerance is 1e-6 instead of 1e-9, so a start a millionth outside a bound is accepted.
Student error r4-01: the lower-bound multipliers are reported with the sign flipped, so non-negative multipliers come out non-positive.
Student error r4-02: the turnover_plus and turnover_minus multipliers are swapped in the output.
Student error r4-03: the budget multiplier is reported with the opposite sign, as if the budget were written one minus the sum.
Student error r4-04: the starting-portfolio budget check uses a tolerance of 1e-6 instead of 1e-9, so a starting sum 2e-9 off the budget is accepted.
Student error r4-05: the turnover limit is applied to the sum of absolute weights, measured from zero rather than from the starting portfolio, in the solver's sign constraints.
Student error r4-06: only the cap of sector 0 enters the search, so the other sector caps are never imposed.
Student error r5-01: the solver's Hessian is Sigma without gamma, so the solution is the minimizer for gamma = 1.
Student error r5-02: the certificate's weight stationarity subtracts the sector multiplier where the page adds it.
Student error r5-03: the starting-portfolio budget is checked by exact equality, so a sum inside the 1e-9 tolerance is refused.
Student error r5-04: the risk-aversion check refuses only negative values, so gamma = 0 is accepted.
Student error r5-05: the returned weights are rounded to six decimals, so the budget and stationarity residuals are about 1e-7.
Student error r7_01: each sector cap is measured from the starting sector weight, so the cap is loosened by the starting sector sum.
Student error r7_02: the starting weights are checked against their box bounds with a tolerance of 1e-8, not the 1e-9 the page states.
Student error r7_03: gamma is refused below one millionth, although the page accepts any positive gamma (the suite tests one billionth).
Student error r7_04: a negative multiplier removes the first working constraint, not the one with the most negative multiplier.
Student error r7_05: each sector cap is written as a lower bound on the sector sum (the inequality sign is reversed).

Student error r7_06: on a degenerate two-asset case (lower = upper = start, zero turnover) the answer reports the dual residual without the floor at zero, with all-positive multipliers; the reference is otherwise unchanged.
Student error r8m01: the starting-sum check refuses only a sum above one, so a start 2e-9 below one is accepted.
Student error r8m02: a lower bound equal to its upper bound is refused as out of order, so the boundary is rejected.
Student error r8m03: the returned weights are rounded to six decimals, so the stationarity residual is about 1e-7.
Student error r8m04: the turnover rows measure the change from zero (sum of signed weights at most tau), not from w0.
Student error r8m05: each sector cap is applied to every asset of the sector separately, not to the sector sum.
Student error r8m06: a risk aversion of exactly zero is accepted, although the page requires gamma to be positive.
Student error s01: positive definiteness is checked on the diagonal only, so an indefinite Sigma is accepted.
Student error s02: a sector cap with no asset in it is never checked, so the extra cap is accepted.
Student error s03: the starting sector weight is compared with its cap without the 1e-9 tolerance.
Student error s04: a turnover limit of exactly zero is refused, so the zero-turnover case is lost.
Student error s05: the starting-portfolio tolerance is 1e-10, so a sum off by 5e-10 is refused.
Student error s06: a missing turnover_limit field is read as zero instead of refused.
Student error s07: a NaN or infinite scalar is silently read as zero instead of refused.
Student error s08: gamma must exceed 1e-5, so the valid boundary gamma equal to 1e-6 is refused.
Student error s09: a lower bound equal to its upper bound is refused as if the order were strict.
Student error s10: the highest sector label is refused (labels accepted only below K minus 1).
Student error s12_01: the turnover-variable stationarity residual uses plus plus minus instead of plus minus minus.
Student error s12_02: the returned weights are rounded to six decimals before the certificate is written.
Silent fallback: a NaN expected return is replaced by zero instead of being refused with ValueError.
Only the first sector cap is imposed in the solver; the second sector cap is never applied.
Starting-portfolio checks use a tolerance of 1e-5, where the page states 1e-9.
The returned weights are rounded to six decimals before the certificate is computed from them.
Silent truncation: an expected-return list one entry longer than the asset count is cut to the matrix size.
The starting portfolio is not checked against the sector caps, so a starting breach is accepted.
The turnover-variable stationarity residual in the certificate uses minus kappa.
Student error v10_03: the turnover-variable stationarity residual adds the two turnover multipliers to the total instead of subtracting them, a sign slip in the certificate.
Student error v11_02: the primal residual uses w_i - l_i for the lower bound, not l_i - w_i, so a feasible point reports a large primal residual.
Student error v11_03: the weight stationarity residual adds the turnover-minus multiplier and subtracts the turnover-plus one.
Student error v14_01: the turnover sign forms are relaxed by 1e-7, so the turnover limit is exceeded by up to 1e-7.
Student error v14_02: the active-set search returns at the first KKT step even when a working multiplier is negative, so dual feasibility is not enforced.
Student error v14_03: the budget multiplier reported is scaled by gamma, which is wrong for gamma other than one.
Student error v6_03: the complementary-slackness residual evaluates the bound rows at the starting portfolio w0 instead of at the returned weights.
Student error v6_04: the certificate's weight stationarity uses 2 gamma Sigma w - mu, the gradient of gamma w' Sigma w - mu' w, which drops the one half of the objective.
Student error v6_05: the turnover sign forms are enumerated with the last asset always counted as a buy, so a sale of the last asset is never limited by the turnover constraint.
Student error v6_06: a turnover limit of exactly zero is read as no limit, so the turnover sign constraints are dropped and the zero-turnover case is solved without them.
Student error v8-01: a debug print runs when the turnover limit is zero, so the answer is not silent on that input.
Student error v8-02: the starting weights are rescaled in place to sum exactly to one, so the argument is changed.
Student error v8-03: the budget multiplier is hard-coded to zero whenever the answer equals the starting portfolio.
Student error v9_01: allocate prints a trace line whenever the turnover limit binds (within 1e-9), a debugging print left in.
Student error v9_02: allocate prints a trace line only for a five-asset case in which the turnover limit binds.
Student error v9_03: allocate emits a warning for a degenerate box (a lower bound equal to its upper bound), and the answer is unchanged.
Student error v9_04: allocate stores a note in its argument when a lower bound equals its upper bound (a cache left in the caller's case).
Student error v9_05: allocate returns a different budget multiplier on every second call with the same case (a module-level counter left in).
Student error v9_06: allocate prints a line before it refuses a boolean sector label (a refusal is allowed, a print is not).
Student error v9_07: allocate writes a note into its argument and then refuses text in mu with TypeError (a refusal is allowed, a change to the argument is not).
Student error v9_08: allocate takes a second, optional argument (tolerance), so its signature is not the one-argument contract of the page.
Student error w01: the starting-portfolio sum is accepted to a tolerance of 1e-8, where the page states 1e-9.
Student error w02: the sector multiplier enters the certificate's stationarity residual with a minus sign.
Student error w03: a risk aversion below 1e-5 is refused as not positive, so the valid gamma of 1e-6 is lost.
Student error w04: the total turnover multiplier is split evenly between the plus and minus multipliers, ignoring the sign of each displacement.
Student error w06: the turnover limit is written as one signed sum of displacements, so only the all-plus sign form is imposed.
Student error w07: a sector_caps list with one cap too many is cut to the number of sector labels, so a cap for an empty sector is silently ignored.
Student error x01: the starting weight is compared with the upper bound without the 1e-9 tolerance.
Student error x02: a sector label equal to the number of caps is accepted (range check one too loose).
Student error x03: each sector cap is compared with the cumulative start weight of sectors 0 to k, not its own sector.
Student error x3-01: allocate caches its first answer per number of assets and returns it for any later case with the same count.
Student error x3-02: the sector cap is written with the wrong sign, so each sector sum must be at least its cap.
Student error x3-03: every upper weight bound is loosened by 1e-7, a tolerance applied to the bound rather than to the check.
Student error y01: a gamma of at most 1e-9 is refused as not positive, so a small valid gamma is lost.
Student error y02: a gamma down to minus 1e-9 is accepted, so a slightly negative risk aversion passes.
Student error y03: a turnover limit down to minus 1e-9 is accepted, so only clearly negative limits fail.
Student error y04: a turnover limit of exactly zero is refused, so the valid boundary is lost.
Student error y05: a lower bound above its upper bound is accepted when the excess is at most 1e-9.
Student error y06: the lower-above-upper check looks at asset 0 only, so a later asset passes.
Student error y07: symmetry of sigma is checked for the pair (0, 1) only, so an asymmetric later pair passes.
Student error y08: a sector label of minus one is read as the last sector (negative indexing).
Student error y09: the starting weight may exceed its upper bound by 1e-8, not the 1e-9 the page states.
Student error y10: the starting sector caps are checked for sector 0 only, so a later breach passes.
Student error z01: the starting weights are compared with the bounds with no 1e-9 tolerance, so a start 5e-10 outside a bound is refused although the page allows it.
Student error z02: the starting sector sums are compared with the caps with no tolerance, so a start that sits 5e-10 over a cap is refused although the page allows it.
Student error z03: allocate prints a progress line before it returns, which the page's silence rule forbids.
Student error z04: allocate writes a cache key into the instance it receives, so the argument changes.
Student error z06: the sector multiplier enters the weight stationarity with the wrong sign in the certificate.
Student error z07: allocate returns the weights in reverse asset order, so each weight is paired with the wrong asset.
Student error z08: the turnover limit is measured from an equal-weight portfolio instead of the starting portfolio w0.
